set_title: Broncho- names: bronchiolitis, bronchiolitis obliterans, bronchopulmonary dysplasia and their look-alikes
stem: A 4-month-old boy, born at term, has had a runny nose for 3 days and now has a cough, fast breathing and poor feeding. It is January, and his older sister has a cold. He has nasal flaring, intercostal retractions, and wheezes and fine crackles over both lungs.
oneliner: 4-month-old boy, term, winter + 3 days of runny nose, then cough, retractions, wheeze and crackles → ?

whyNot.B: Bronchiolitis obliterans is fixed scarring of the small airways after a transplant, a severe infection or toxic fumes; he has a **3-day illness that began as a cold**
whyNot.C: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia follows preterm birth with weeks of ventilation and oxygen; he was **born at term**
whyNot.D: Bronchiectasis is permanent airway widening with years of purulent sputum; his illness is **3 days old and began with a runny nose**
whyNot.E: Bronchogenic cyst is a congenital mediastinal mass with focal signs; he has **wheezes and crackles over both lungs during a winter cold**

why: bronchiol = small airway and -itis = inflammation: a short viral infection of the bronchioles. **A winter cold in an infant that moves down to wheeze, crackles and retractions** is bronchiolitis, and RSV causes most cases. Care is supportive; palivizumab or nirsevimab, antibodies against the RSV F (fusion) protein, prevent it in high-risk infants.

What it is
Classic patient
One clue
rows: Bronchiolitis
bronchiol = small airway; -itis = inflammation
Acute viral infection of the bronchioles, most often RSV
Infant under 2 years in winter: a runny nose for a few days, then cough, fast breathing and wheeze
**Infant with a cold that moves down to wheeze, crackles and retractions**
Bronchiolitis obliterans
bronchiol = small airway; -itis = inflammation; obliterans = closing off
Scar tissue that plugs and closes the small airways, giving fixed airflow obstruction
Lung transplant recipient months to years later (chronic rejection); also after stem cell transplant with GVHD, adenovirus or Mycoplasma in a child, or toxic fumes
**Steady fall in FEV1 that does not reverse with a bronchodilator, with air trapping on CT**
Bronchopulmonary dysplasia
broncho = airway; pulmonary = lung; dys = abnormal; -plasia = growth
Chronic lung disease of prematurity: oxygen and ventilator injury halts alveolar growth
Preterm infant who needed mechanical ventilation and oxygen and still needs oxygen weeks later
**Born very preterm, ventilated, still oxygen-dependent at 36 weeks postmenstrual age**
Bronchiectasis
bronchi = airways; ectasis = widening
Permanent widening of the bronchi from repeated infection and inflammation with poor mucus clearance
Cystic fibrosis, primary ciliary dyskinesia, or an old severe pneumonia
**Daily cough with large volumes of purulent sputum; airways wider than their arteries on CT**
Bronchogenic cyst
broncho = airway; -genic = arising from; cyst = fluid sac
Congenital fluid-filled cyst from abnormal budding of the foregut airway
Often an incidental finding; can compress the trachea or a bronchus
**Round, fluid-density mass in the middle mediastinum near the carina**
Bronchopulmonary sequestration
broncho = airway; pulmonary = lung; sequestration = set apart
Nonfunctioning lung tissue with no connection to the airways, fed by a systemic artery
Child or young adult with repeated pneumonia in the same lower lobe, usually the left
**Feeding artery that comes off the aorta**

idea.rule: Bronchiolitis = acute and viral in infants; bronchiolitis obliterans = chronic scar after transplant, infection or fumes. Same root, opposite time course.
also: RSV is an enveloped negative-sense RNA virus (a paramyxovirus in classic teaching) that enters cells through its F (fusion) protein
Peaks in winter in children under 2; preterm infants and those with heart or lung disease do worst
Treatment is supportive: suction, oxygen, fluids

set_title: Broncho- names: bronchiolitis, bronchiolitis obliterans, bronchopulmonary dysplasia and their look-alikes
stem: A 3-month-old boy was born at 26 weeks' gestation and needed surfactant, mechanical ventilation and supplemental oxygen for 8 weeks. He still needs oxygen through a nasal cannula, breathes fast, and gains weight slowly. A chest x-ray shows coarse streaky opacities mixed with overinflated areas in both lungs. He has had no fever.
oneliner: 3-month-old boy born at 26 weeks + 8 weeks of ventilation and oxygen + still oxygen-dependent, streaky lungs → ?

whyNot.A: Bronchiolitis obliterans scars the airways after a transplant, a severe infection or toxic fumes; his lung disease traces to **birth at 26 weeks with 8 weeks on a ventilator and oxygen**
whyNot.B: Bronchiolitis is a short viral infection with a runny nose and fever; he has **needed oxygen since birth and has had no fever**
whyNot.C: Bronchopulmonary sequestration is one segment of lung fed by a systemic artery; his changes are **in both lungs** and follow ventilator care
whyNot.D: Bronchiectasis brings years of purulent sputum, usually in older children and adults; he is **3 months old with ongoing oxygen need since a preterm birth**

why: broncho = airway, pulmonary = lung, dys = abnormal, -plasia = growth: the lung did not grow normally. **A very preterm infant who was ventilated and given oxygen and still needs oxygen weeks later** has bronchopulmonary dysplasia. Oxygen free radicals and pressure injure the immature lung and halt alveolar growth, so the alveoli stay fewer and larger.

set_title: Broncho- names: bronchiolitis, bronchiolitis obliterans, bronchopulmonary dysplasia and their look-alikes
stem: A 47-year-old woman has had a daily cough for 3 years that brings up large amounts of thick, foul-smelling yellow sputum, sometimes streaked with blood. She had a severe pneumonia at age 30. She has clubbing and coarse crackles at both lung bases. CT shows thick-walled airways in both lower lobes that are wider than the arteries beside them.
oneliner: 47F + 3 years of daily cough with copious purulent sputum + clubbing + airways wider than arteries in both lower lobes → ?

whyNot.A: Bronchogenic cyst is a single fluid-filled mass near the carina; she has **widened airways in both lower lobes**
whyNot.B: Bronchiolitis obliterans closes small airways and gives a dry cough with air trapping; she has **large amounts of purulent sputum and dilated airways**
whyNot.C: Bronchopulmonary sequestration is one segment of lung cut off from the airways; she has **dilated airways in both lower lobes**, not one disconnected segment
whyNot.E: Bronchiolitis is a short viral illness of infants; she is **47 with a 3-year cough**

why: bronchi = airways, ectasis = widening: the airways are permanently dilated. **Years of daily cough with large volumes of purulent sputum, clubbing, and airways wider than their arteries on CT** is bronchiectasis. Infection and inflammation destroy the muscle and elastic tissue of the airway wall, and poor clearance keeps the cycle going.

Can cause hemoptysis and secondary amyloidosis
